review_notes:
I read the whole file and looked for repeated proof arguments that are substantial and in different results. I found three kinds of repetition. None of them justifies a new helper lemma.

1. `contractLeft_contractLeft`, `contractLeft_comm`, `changeForm_contractLeft`, `changeForm_self_apply` and `changeForm_changeForm`, plus `map_add'` and `map_smul'` in `contractLeft`, all use the `CliffordAlgebra.left_induction` skeleton. Each has an `algebraMap` case, an `add` case and an `ι_mul` case. The `algebraMap` and `add` cases are one-line rewrites. The `ι_mul` cases differ in their algebra, so they share no common statement. Factoring out the skeleton would only save a few words.

2. The `contractRight_*` lemmas (`contractRight_mul_ι`, `contractRight_ι`, `contractRight_algebraMap`, `contractRight_contractRight`, `contractRight_comm`) are each a short transfer through `contractRight_eq` and `reverse`. They are already one to three rewrites each, so a helper would not shorten them.

3. The side-condition term `fun m x fx ↦ contractLeftAux_contractLeftAux Q d m x fx` appears three times, in `contractLeft_ι_mul`, `contractLeft_ι` and `contractLeft_algebraMap`. It is a one-line argument, so this is a repeated one-line application and does not meet the rubric.

The two aux-squared lemmas, `contractLeftAux_contractLeftAux` and `changeFormAux_changeFormAux`, have similar rewrite chains. They involve different operators and different terms, so they do not share a natural abstraction.

I did not search the rest of Mathlib for existing induction helpers, because I found no justified repeat to propose.
